project.name: GameTime
project.description: GameTime is a personal accountability iOS app: one person commits to a seven-day steps goal and a test commitment, the client reads Apple Health merged step totals, and authenticated daily snapshots are scored on a Supabase backend. Note: this project has over 100 source files; consider scoping analysis to a subdirectory for faster results.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with README.md to see what GameTime is today: one person commits to a seven-day steps goal and a test commitment, the iPhone reads Apple Health merged step totals, and authenticated daily snapshots are scored on Supabase. The document also maps what already works on a physical device against the local stack versus what remains behind Stage B gates. Treat this as the product map before you open any Swift or SQL.

tour.title: iOS App Entry
tour.description: GameTimeApp.swift is the SwiftUI @main entry. It boots Sign in with Apple, onboarding, and the signed-in shell around personal-accountability state rather than a competitive social graph. Reading this file after the README shows how a Debug run on a physical iPhone actually starts.
tour.languageLesson: SwiftUI apps declare a single App type with @main. The Scene you return (usually WindowGroup) is the process root; environment objects injected here reach every later view.

tour.title: Session and Shell
tour.description: Building on the app entry, AppModel owns launch phase, Sign in with Apple, and onboarding, while AppShellView is the signed-in chrome: Today, Challenges, and You tabs plus foreground refresh. Together they are the runtime coordinator that later Health and challenge stores attach to.

tour.title: Personal Challenge Domain
tour.description: PersonalAccountabilityModels defines cadence, drafts, frozen terms, and daily progress types; PersonalAccountabilityStore loads challenges and drives create, cancel, payment, and refresh. This is the client vocabulary for the seven-day commitment the README described, sitting between the shell in Step 3 and Health reads next.
tour.languageLesson: Codable structs in Swift encode the API contract. An ObservableObject (or @Observable) store keeps UI in sync when challenge lists and payment state change.

tour.title: Apple Health Snapshots
tour.description: HealthKitActivityClient queries Apple Health merged step statistics. PersonalHealthStepReader plans daily windows and builds snapshot payloads; PersonalStepSnapshot resolves what the UI should show by merging local days with server-frozen results. New Personal challenges use this daily non-manual path rather than hourly App Attest coverage.
tour.languageLesson: HealthKit returns HKStatistics over date intervals. The client must treat Apple's merged total as source of truth and drop only samples Apple marks as manually entered.

tour.title: Shared Core Types
tour.description: GameTimeCore is the shared Swift package used by the iPhone app. HealthSample classifies HealthKit provenance for contest-era metric trust, which still matters for historical Personal challenges that keep attested_hourly_v1. Understanding this package explains why scoring types live outside SwiftUI views.

tour.title: Sync and Upload
tour.description: PersonalHealthBackgroundDelivery registers Health observers so step changes can wake the pipeline, while PersonalHealthSnapshotUploader posts authenticated daily snapshots to Supabase (with a disabled no-op for unsigned builds). This is the bridge from local snapshots in Step 5 to the Edge API in the next steps.

tour.title: Commit Edge Function
tour.description: personal-challenge-commit is the Deno Edge Function that finalizes a seven-day challenge after JWT auth and Stripe sandbox SetupIntent checks. The index file wires env and adapters; the handler enforces payment terms before rows exist. This is the server counterpart to the store's create flow from Step 4.
tour.languageLesson: Supabase Edge Functions are Deno.serve handlers. The index.ts file is a thin composition root; handler.ts holds the authenticated business rules so they can be unit-tested without the HTTP shell.

tour.title: Shared API Primitives
tour.description: jwt.ts is the highest fan-in backend module: almost every function verifies a Supabase Bearer token here. database.ts wraps PostgREST service RPCs for personal challenges, device keys, and related writes. These shared adapters are why Edge Functions stay small after Step 8.

tour.title: Personal Data Schema
tour.description: The Personal V1 backend migration creates challenge terms, results, and the older coverage and eligibility-hold tables. The Health snapshot v2 migration adds daily progress tables and cutover RPCs so scoring no longer depends on those holds. This is the Postgres contract the store, uploader, and commit function all write into.
tour.languageLesson: Postgres migrations are ordered, append-only SQL. Later files add tables and RPCs without rewriting earlier ones, so historical hourly Personal rows can coexist with snapshot-v2 daily rows.

tour.title: Copy and Decisions
tour.description: docs/COPY.md is the spoken-English contract for every on-screen string: no evidence, coverage, or framework names. DECISIONS.md is the append-only log of stack, scoring, and Personal Health snapshot choices. After you have seen the client and schema, these docs explain why the UI never says the words the code uses.

tour.title: Tests and CI
tour.description: PersonalStepProgressV2Tests lock DST, cache, and displayed-progress behavior for the snapshot path in Step 5. GameTimeUITests fail if competitive-social vocabulary leaks onto screen, matching COPY.md. The GitHub Actions workflow runs pgTAP, Deno Edge tests, GameTimeCore on Linux, and Xcode product tests so those contracts stay true on every push.
tour.languageLesson: GitHub Actions workflows use on triggers, jobs for parallel work, and steps for sequential commands. This pipeline splits database, Deno, and Xcode so a Swift UI copy failure does not hide a Postgres scoring regression.
